newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium ends mixed in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium ends mixed in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures closed mixed after lacklustre trade on Thursday as speculators shifted attention to highly volatile precious metals markets, traders said.

"There're no fresh incentives," said one trader at a major trading house. "The rise on the LME overnight was offset by the dollar's decline (compared to Wednesday)," he said. "Precious metals are more interesting at the moment."
TOCOM benchmark April 1998 closed up 0.1 yen at 196.8 yen per kg. Other contracts ranged between from 1.2 yen weaker to 0.5 yen higher.
Estimated trade volume shrank to 1,902 lots, the second lowest since Tokyo aluminium futures were launched on April 7.

Traders said the dollar's rise to above 116 yen in the afternoon following sluggish Japanese industrial production data triggered some buying after a very quiet morning session when no October and December contracts changed hands.
